title: Northstar GPU runway playbook — NA/EU/APAC 2027 forecast
content:
Executive summary:
This playbook outlines a practical, staged runway for GPU activation across North America, Europe, and APAC for calendar 2027. Focus is on matching expected workload shapes (bursty gen + steady embeddings/ranking), keeping a small but hot warm-pool for low-latency SLOs, and a configurable surge path that favors H100 for high-throughput model classes and A100/NVIDIA-equivalents for embedding/cheaper inference.

Key objectives:
- Keep p95 token latency under 220ms for hosted tier in NA/EU and under 260ms in APAC during steady state.
- Maintain gross fleet utilization target 55%-70% (region-specific).
- Preserve a warm-pool equal to 6%–12% of active fleet to absorb burst windows without cold start penalty.
- Stage rollouts to minimize cross-region dependency and allow fallbacks (compatible quantized variants).

Assumptions and inputs:
- Base forecast demand derived from Q2–Q3 2026 traffic growth, product roadmaps (chat + vector search), and anticipated enterprise onboarding cadence.
- Hardware mix options: H100 (preferred for large-gen), A100-80GB (balanced), and T4/RTX6000-class (cost lanes for embeddings and lightweight ops).
- Cloud regions: NA (us-west-2, us-east-1), EU (eu-west-1, eu-central-1), APAC (ap-northeast-1, ap-southeast-1).
- Timeline granularity: monthly for first 9 months of ramp, then quarterly.

Notes on normalization: EGPU approximates H100 capacity. A100 counts as 0.6 EGPU for large-gen but 0.85 for embedding workloads (we schedule by dominant workload type per fleet pool).

Warm-pool strategy:
- Warm-pool composition: primarily A100 + a small cushion of H100 for single-token-latency-sensitive routes.
- Target warm-pool sizes: NA 8% of active fleet, EU 9%, APAC 10% initially (higher APAC because of regional latency variability).
- Warm-pool warming cadence: keep warm VMs for baseline; blue-green micro-rotation every 6 hours to prevent drift.

Rollout timeline and activation windows (high level):
- Phase 0 (Jan–Mar 2027): validate provisioning pipelines in NA (us-west-2 primary). Ramp 40% of the initial runway and run two canaries: one for embedding-heavy models, one for conversational-gen.
- Phase 1 (Mar–May 2027): full NA ramp to planned baseline; enable autoscaling hooks tied to request-rate and observed per-model token-per-request distributions.
- Phase 2 (May–Aug 2027): EU activation in staggered waves by cloud-zone (eu-west-1 first, eu-central-1 second). Maintain cross-region fallbacks to NA for non-PII routes for 48–72 hours post-activation.
- Phase 3 (Jul–Oct 2027): APAC carousel rollout with conservative warm-pool buffer; enable regional KV cache priming for commonly used prompt prefixes.

Surge response lanes and thresholds:
- Minor surge (<= 15% over baseline): auto-burst to warm-pool; no reservations used.
- Moderate surge (15%–40%): activate queued reserved instances and leaky-bucket smoothing; shift lower-priority batch jobs to cheaper SKUs for 12–24 hours.
- Major surge (>40% or sustained >20% for 6+ hours): trigger cross-region spill (EU <-> NA), notify SRE and Account teams, and enable emergency procurement channel (see linked JIRA).

Quality and observability hooks:
- Dashboards: per-region p50/p95/p99 token latencies; per-model throughput; warm-pool fill-rate; autoscaler lag histogram.
- Regression gating: daily evals on benchmark prompt set for top-20 customer models; if embedding cosine-drop > 0.02 or generation BLEU-style drift > threshold, pause rollout and rollback to nearest pinned model.

Risk matrix (top risks and mitigations):
- GPU supply delays (risk: high) -> mitigation: stagger orders across vendors, keep >8 weeks spot buffer, maintain convertible A100 order fallback.
- Unexpected workload shift (risk: medium) -> mitigation: dynamic model re-routing policies, conservative initial util targets, rapid canary for affected customers.
- Networking/backplane congestion (risk: medium-high for APAC) -> mitigation: localized KV-cache priming, CDN routing adjustments, abortable prefetch.

Action items (owners and ETA):
- Finalize normalized EGPU conversion table (owner: Jinsoo Park) — ETA 2026-10-10
- Provision warm-pool templates across 6 target zones (owner: Miguel Alvarez) — ETA 2026-10-20
- Add surge automation playbooks to runbooks repo (owner: Aisha Thompson) — ETA 2026-10-05
- Dry-run canary in us-west-2 with embedding workload (owner: Priya Kaur) — ETA 2026-11-01

Open questions / decision points:
- Do we commit to H100-heavy purchase for Q3 2027 or keep flexible convertible orders? (tradeoff: cost vs. speed of activation)
- What is the regional SLA delta that justifies a higher warm-pool in APAC vs EU? Need product input.

Appendix: quick-reference capacity knobs (for on-call):
- ScaleUpPct: percentage to provision when sustained util > target for 30m
- WarmPoolPct: immediate available non-evictable pool size
- ColdStartDelay: TTL for evicted KV caches (lower for embeddings)
- FallbackRoutePriority: numeric order for cross-region fallbacks

This doc is a working playbook — comments welcome inline. Link to related procurement notes and the canary run checklist in linked_artifacts.
